summary:
MARVIN is an interactive website that lets users plan a human expedition through Jezero Crater on Mars. It combines NASA maps, rover imagery, and terrain data to help users explore the landscape, select science activities, and create a round-trip route from a concept Martian base. Users can add stops and adjust their plans based on distance, available time, and terrain steepness, while 3D views and real Perseverance panoramas bring the surroundings to life.

Once a route is ready, users can simulate the walk, track progress, and practice responding to emergencies such as dust storms or equipment problems. Mission plans can also be saved or printed. MARVIN turns scattered scientific data into an accessible exploration tool, showing how it could support future astronauts. It remains a prototype, with simulated emergency scenarios and estimated conditions rather than live mission guidance.
details:
MARVIN (Mars Astronaut Route Visualization Intelligence Navigator) helps users plan a human expedition through Jezero Crater. It combines NASA imagery, elevation data, rover locations, and historical panoramas in one interactive map. Users choose science activities, add destinations, and generate round-trip routes based on time, distance, and slope limits. They can then simulate their walk, explore 3D terrain, practice emergency responses, and export their plans. Our goal is to make complex Mars data easier to understand while demonstrating how future explorers could balance scientific discovery with a safe return.

We built MARVIN using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for 3D visualization and Esri services for terrain exploration. Its terrain AI uses an NVIDIA SegFormer-B0 backbone trained on AI4Mars images and runs in the browser through ONNX Runtime Web. Our creative approach connects route planning, science recommendations, immersive imagery, and emergency simulations in one experience. Throughout development, we considered terrain steepness, walking effort, mission duration, return reserves, browser performance, and data availability. We also distinguish measured observations from estimates: MARVIN is an educational prototype, and its simulated hazards and routes are not certified for real astronaut missions.
